head: Some Galaxy phones report Android Auto and battery trouble on One UI 9
dek: Since Samsung's Android 17-based One UI 9 update started reaching older Galaxy phones, some owners report Android Auto stuttering or not connecting, and others report batteries draining fast. Google says a fix for the Android Auto problem is rolling out.
details: 9to5Google says the Android Auto reports aren't widespread but show a clear pattern; in one user's test, a Galaxy S24 Ultra on One UI 9 had the problem and a Galaxy S25 Edge on One UI 8.5 didn't. Battery complaints come from Galaxy S24 and S25 owners, including one who says the phone now needs charging three to four times a day; many others see no change. Update: Google told Android Authority that a fix for the Android Auto problem is rolling out to affected Android 17 and One UI 9 phones.
where: Galaxy phones updated to One UI 9
means: If Android Auto or your battery got worse right after the One UI 9 update, you're not the only one, and it's likely the update.
todo: Restart the phone and check which apps use the most power under battery settings. A big update can drain more for a few days while the phone finishes background work. Install Samsung's next update when it arrives.
